ip_address: The wire `.id` maps to computed Terraform `id`; `vrf` is read-only because the pinned target rejects it as writable. Bare IP writes use an explicit host prefix; semantically equivalent readback preserves configured spelling.
Use a disconnected test bridge or an unused interface for experiments, not the management interface.
interface_bridge: Configuring `pvid` requires explicit `vlan_filtering = true`; RouterOS hides PVID otherwise. VLAN filtering can disrupt connectivity: do not experiment on a management bridge.
interface_bridge_port: Attach only an unused interface in a test topology; moving a management port into a bridge can disconnect the router.
interface_vlan: VLAN IDs must be 1–4094 and MTU must be 68–65535. The parent interface must already exist; use Terraform references for dependencies.
interface_list: Explicit empty `include` and `exclude` strings clear those memberships. Built-in interface lists cannot be managed.
interface_list_member: Use references to managed interface/list names to establish dependencies; no automatic renaming of dependent objects is promised.
ip_pool: `ranges` is a required nonempty, non-overlapping list of IPv4 addresses or ascending `start-end` ranges; IPv6 and CIDR are rejected. Equivalent numeric ranges preserve configured order/single-IP spelling; import adopts the server representation. Missing `next_pool` reads as `none`.
ip_dhcp_server: The reviewed server fields do not include lease scripts, time-format settings or option attachments. Client/server option definitions, option sets/matchers, relays and DHCP-client resources are available separately; their availability does not add attributes to this server schema.
`address_pool` is required. Omitted `add_arp` reads as false and omitted `conflict_detection` as true. Live acceptance keeps the server disabled and does not certify actual DHCP exchanges.
ip_dhcp_server_lease: Only static leases are managed; dynamic leases are rejected rather than converted. MAC addresses require 48 bits. Equivalent configured case/separator spelling is preserved; import adopts canonical remote spelling. Omitted `block_access` reads as false.
Lease scripts, time-format settings and option attachments are not in this schema. DHCP exchange behavior is not certified.
ip_dhcp_server_network: `address` requires canonical IPv4 CIDR, `gateway` and DNS entries are IPv4, and `netmask` is 0–32. `dns_server = []` clears the list; `dns_none = true` cannot be combined with nonempty DNS servers. Omitted DNS/domain read as empty and omitted `dns_none` as false.
DHCP option resources are available separately, but option attachments and script/time-format settings are not attributes of this network resource.
ip_route: Requires explicit canonical IPv4 destination CIDR and gateway; no implicit default route. Only explicitly static records are managed; missing static metadata fails closed. Distance is 1–255 and scopes are 0–255. Blackhole/presence-sensitive flags and dynamic routes are not exposed.
ip_firewall_addr_list: Permanent IPv4 address/canonical CIDR/ascending-range entries only; DNS, IPv6 and finite lifetimes are excluded from this resource. Equivalent numeric configured spelling is retained; import adopts remote canonical spelling. IPv6 address-list entries have a separate resource.
ip_firewall_filter: Reviewed actions are accept/drop/log/passthrough/return. Jump/reject/fasttrack/add-to-list and their dependent fields are not exposed.

`place_before` accepts a same-chain static internal `*HEX` ID; explicit empty string means chain end. Omitted placement is unmanaged. Readback reports the next same-chain rule, and external moves produce drift. Dynamic chains, self/missing/cross-chain anchors and malformed snapshots fail closed; REST provides no transaction/global ordering lock.
ip_firewall_nat: Reviewed actions are accept/log/passthrough/return/masquerade/src-nat/dst-nat. Source/destination NAT requires `to_addresses` as IPv4 address or ascending range, not CIDR/DNS/IPv6. Nonempty targets for unrelated actions are rejected; port/protocol matchers and advanced NAT actions are not exposed.

`place_before` uses a same-chain static `*HEX` anchor; explicit empty string means chain end, and omitted placement is unmanaged. Dynamic chains and unsafe anchors are rejected. No traffic-translation certification or global ordering transaction is claimed.
ip_firewall_mangle: Reviewed actions are accept/log/passthrough/return/mark-connection/mark-packet. Mark actions require the corresponding nonempty `new_connection_mark` or `new_packet_mark`; configured marks must match the action. `passthrough` is authorized only for those two mark actions. Routing marks, DSCP/MSS/TTL changes and sniffing are not exposed.

`place_before` uses a same-chain static `*HEX` anchor; explicit empty string means chain end, and omitted placement is unmanaged. No traffic-marking certification or global ordering transaction is claimed.
ip_firewall_raw: Reviewed actions are accept/drop/log/notrack/passthrough/return. Jump and add-to-list are not exposed. `place_before` uses a same-chain static `*HEX` anchor; explicit empty string means chain end, and omitted placement is unmanaged. No traffic/notrack certification or global ordering transaction is claimed.
ip_dhcp_client_option: `code` is 1–254. `value` is a required nonempty RouterOS expression, sent unchanged; `raw_value` is read-only. Built-in options with `default=true` cannot be adopted. Names require replacement; code/value updates are in place. No full expression/script grammar or DHCP exchange is certified.
ip_dhcp_server_option: `code` is 1–254. `value` is a required nonempty RouterOS expression, sent unchanged; `raw_value` is read-only. Names require replacement; code/value updates are in place. Omitted `comment` reads as empty and omitted `force` as false. No full expression/script grammar or DHCP exchange is certified.
ip_dhcp_relay: The reviewed contract uses a replacement-owned name, an interface, unique canonical IPv4 server destinations and an automatic local address of `0.0.0.0`. Option-82 payloads and duration fields are not exposed. Live configuration tests keep the relay disabled.
ip_dns_record: Only named A/AAAA records are supported; name/type changes require replacement. Hostnames and address family must be canonical and consistent. Unmanaged regex/address-list behavior is rejected. Omitted `match_subdomain` reads as false.
interface_veth: Requires a hash-bound matching extra publication during generation and an enabled matching-version container package at runtime. Base publication paths are never fabricated. Configuration testing does not execute containers.
system_user_sshkeys: Mutation is replacement-only; item PATCH is unsupported. Only reviewed ssh-ed25519, ssh-rsa and ecdsa-sha2-nistp256 public keys without authorized-key options are accepted. SHA256 fingerprint ownership is verified, including RouterOS padding.

Administrator and authenticated-user keys cannot be managed. Import cannot recover public-key material; supplying a key after fresh import requires replacement. Omitted/masked key material preserves known state, while unrelated fingerprints are rejected.
ip_ipsec_policy_group: Only a meaningful replacement-owned name is exposed; the purported comment field is unsupported by RouterOS.
tool_netwatch: Existing objects with nonempty, hidden/masked or malformed up/down/test callbacks cannot be managed through this subset. No arbitrary callback execution is certified.
system_user: The administrator and currently authenticated user cannot be managed. The required sensitive password is not printed in diagnostics; protect Terraform state.
system_user_group: Built-in full/read/write groups cannot be managed. Permission lists account for explicit negative flags in RouterOS readback.
ip_cloud: The pinned targets accept `ddns_enabled = auto` or `yes`, not `no`. Configuration acceptance does not certify external DDNS communication.
disk_settings: `auto_media_interface` is an interface name, not the symbolic interface list `static`; isolated tests use the disconnected `tf-test` bridge.
ip_smb: `interfaces` names actual interfaces; `none` was rejected by the pinned targets. Isolated tests keep SMB disabled and use `tf-test`.
capsman_manager: Live tests keep certificate requirements disabled and exercise reviewed upgrade policies; automatic certificate generation and remote CAP upgrades are not certified.
user_manager_database: Changing `db_path` reloads the database and can reset user-manager settings and advanced options. Manage this resource first and give dependent user-manager resources an explicit `depends_on`. Database contents, relocation safety and migration compatibility are not certified.
user_manager_settings: When managing a database-path change, use `depends_on = [routeros_user_manager_database.example]` so database reload precedes settings changes. `require_message_auth` accepts `no` or `yes-access-request`.
user_manager_advanced: When managing a database-path change, use `depends_on = [routeros_user_manager_database.example]` so database reload precedes advanced-option changes. External payment-provider behavior is not certified.
system_led_settings: Physical LED controls are not supported by CHR: GET returns an empty settings object and control requests report unsupported hardware. Mock/schema coverage is not physical-board live acceptance.
